[PATH:empirical] Systematic simulation of mod-3 cellular automata on random and structured non-uniform initial conditions, systematically varying the proportion and placement of minority states to map the basin of attraction sizes and fixed-point frequencies. — Direct computational experimentation can determine whether the system typically converges to a fixed point or to low-period cycles, and whether this depends on the degree of non-uniformity. This would provide empirical confirmation or refutation of the hypothesis under controlled conditions.

[PATH:theoretical] Analytical reduction of mod-3 state-transition rules to a potential function or Lyapunov function, leveraging known results on monotone and threshold automata over finite lattices. — If the transition rule admits a global Lyapunov function, convergence to a fixed point is guaranteed. Conversely, if no such function exists and the rule is not acyclic, low-period attractors may be inevitable. This theoretical approach can explain the mechanism underlying the observed dynamics.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of known attractor structures in mod-k cellular automata and similar discrete dynamical systems on graphs, with focus on results for non-uniform initial conditions and small state spaces. — Existing work on mod-3 and other mod-k rules (e.g., those studied in the context of cyclic cellular automata) may already characterize conditions for fixed-point versus cyclic attractors. Synthesizing these results can contextualize the hypothesis and identify whether non-uniform initial conditions are known to bias convergence.

qualifier.temporal: under steady-state conditions after sufficient iterations
qualifier.geographic: within simulated community networks with non-uniform initial conditions
